task.title: Harden Emacs chat gateway object and stream cursor boundaries
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/1063 by rejecting absent required gateway objects at their field boundary and tracking decoded SSE consumption with a live marker that follows URL decoder buffer mutations.
acceptance_criteria: An absent required object field fails immediately with vela-chat-error while a present empty JSON object remains valid.
The SSE decoded-body cursor follows insertions and deletions before the consumed point.
Transport teardown detaches the cursor marker without changing existing transport, event, origin, or transcript bounds.
Focused and complete repository verification pass.

attempts.summary: Reproduced absent required-object acceptance with a focused RED regression.
attempts.diagnostic: vela-chat--required-object delegated to vela-chat--field and then used listp. Because listp accepts nil, an absent field was indistinguishable from a present empty object at this boundary.
attempts.patch: Resolve the association itself with assoc-string, require its presence, then validate and return its cdr. Added separate regressions for absent, JSON-null, and present-empty objects.

attempts.summary: Reproduced decoded stream cursor drift with a mutation between polling passes.
attempts.diagnostic: The SSE transport retained the consumed body position as an integer. A decoder-owned deletion before that position left the integer stale and could skip or duplicate later decoded bytes.
attempts.patch: Store the decoded-body position as a marker, advance it with set-marker, and detach it during transport teardown. The production-adapter regression mutates the retrieval buffer between chunks and still receives exactly one complete final event.

attempts.summary: Closed cancellation during SSE event dispatch without dereferencing a detached marker.
attempts.diagnostic: A production-adapter regression cancelled the stream from inside on-event and initially failed with Marker does not point anywhere when polling continued after teardown detached the cursor.
attempts.patch: Dispatch event batches only while the transport is live, guard final cursor checks with done state plus marker-buffer presence, and suppress error callbacks once cancellation has made teardown authoritative. The exact cancellation regression then passed without post-cancel dispatch or error.

attempts.summary: Verified the corrected follow-up candidate through focused and repository-wide gates.
attempts.diagnostic: All 36 focused chat ERT tests passed; the complete Emacs suite passed 120/120; just verify and the all-system no-build flake evaluation passed.
attempts.patch: No further implementation change was required after the strict object and marker corrections.

outcome.summary: Required gateway objects now preserve field presence semantics, and the asynchronous SSE consumer follows decoder-owned buffer movement without retaining killed retrieval buffers.

verification.command: nix develop --command emacs --batch -Q -L emacs -L emacs/tests -l vela-chat-mode-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit

lessons: A decoded nil value cannot by itself prove that a required JSON field was present; validate association presence before validating the field value.
Long-lived consumers of decoder-owned buffers need markers rather than integer positions whenever the decoder may insert or delete text before the cursor.
Markers tied to temporary network buffers must be detached during teardown to avoid retaining killed buffers.
